items.quote: And Pharaoh’s servants said unto him, How long shall this man be a snare unto us? let the men go, that they may serve the LORD their God: knowest thou not yet that Egypt is destroyed?
items.claim: Pharaoh's servants urged him to let the Israelite men go, saying Egypt was already destroyed.
items.action: urged release of the Israelite men
items.mechanism: court advisers pressing the ruler after the plagues had damaged Egypt

items.quote: And Moses and Aaron were brought again unto Pharaoh: and he said unto them, Go, serve the LORD your God: but who are they that shall go?
items.claim: Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh, who agreed they could go and serve their God but asked who exactly would go.
items.action: gave conditional permission and asked who would go
items.mechanism: negotiation over who would be allowed to leave

items.quote: And Moses said, We will go with our young and with our old, with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our herds will we go; for we must hold a feast unto the LORD.
items.claim: Moses demanded that everyone go, young and old, sons and daughters, with their flocks and herds, to hold a feast to the LORD.
items.action: demanded that the whole people and their livestock leave
items.mechanism: religious duty to hold a feast, given as the reason everyone had to go
